issues: Report detail body renders `ai_summary` (the GPT-generated summary), not the raw `highlights` field. After PATCH /reports/{id} updates `highlights`, the change is stored (verified via GET) but is not visible in the detail body area (which still shows the original AI summary). The reviewer's expectation 'highlights persisted in report detail body area' is only true if the user reads the raw fields; consider re-rendering highlights explicitly on the detail screen or regenerating ai_summary after edit.

action_items: Optional: after PATCH /reports/{id} edits highlights/delays/change_orders/material_notes, regenerate ai_summary OR also show the raw editable fields on the report detail screen so edits are visible without opening the edit form. Backend already persists them correctly.
Optional (carried from iteration_2): mock/hide signature pad on web (Platform.OS === 'web') since react-native-signature-canvas depends on react-native-webview which is unsupported on web preview.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1381 lines - split into routers (auth, reports, customers, digest, transcribe, files, visits) for maintainability.

BUG (fixed by testing agent): FastAPI was constructed with `lifespan=lifespan`, which makes `@app.on_event('startup')` and `@app.on_event('shutdown')` NO-OPS. As a result the APScheduler was never attached to `app.scheduler`, and PUT /api/digest/schedule crashed with AttributeError inside _reschedule_digest. Fix (applied): moved scheduler bootstrap + shutdown into the `lifespan` async context manager and removed the redundant on_event handlers.

GET /api/files/{path} accepts a ?token= query param that is a full JWT. That is fine for the intended preview flow, but a leaked URL means any Bearer JWT is now visible in server access logs and browser history. Consider using short-lived, single-purpose signed URLs (separate token with `type: 'file-read'` claim + shorter exp) instead of reusing the auth JWT.
public_report endpoint returns author_name and project_code/name — confirm this is intentional for the 'customer portal' view; a paranoid PM may want to hide the internal role.

rca_of_issue: Bug (fixed by testing agent): PUT /api/digest/schedule returned 500 Internal Server Error. Root cause: server.py defines `app = FastAPI(title=..., lifespan=lifespan)` AND registers `@app.on_event('startup')` handlers. Per FastAPI/Starlette docs, when a `lifespan` context manager is passed, all `on_event('startup'|'shutdown')` handlers are ignored — so `_start_scheduler` never ran and `app.scheduler` was never set, causing `AttributeError: 'FastAPI' object has no attribute 'scheduler'` inside `_reschedule_digest`. Fix applied: moved AsyncIOScheduler creation + `scheduler.start()` + `_reschedule_digest(app)` into the `lifespan` async context manager (before `yield`) and `scheduler.shutdown()` after `yield`; removed the dead `@app.on_event` handlers. Verified: backend logs now show 'apscheduler.scheduler - INFO - Scheduler started' and 'Added job _run_scheduled_digest to job store default' on startup, and PUT /api/digest/schedule returns 200 with the schedule persisted (verified via re-GET). Full pytest re-run: 62/62 green including test_put_schedule_admin.
